title: Treaty Room
subtitle: A sealed research room no one owns
narration: What if rival labs could pool their unpublished results, without trusting anyone to hold them? Meet Treaty Room.

caption: Signs in with Tide. No password ever reaches our server.
narration: Dr Mei Lee runs an Alzheimer's lab at Northbridge University. She signs in with Tide. No password ever lands on our server.

caption: Encrypted in her browser before it's stored.
narration: She opens the consortium room, signs its access policy once in her Tide enclave, and deposits a failed drug result. It's encrypted right in her browser.

caption: Refused. Even her own deposit stays sealed.
narration: Helix and St Aurelia deposit too. Now watch: Mei tries to open the room. Refused. Even her own deposit stays sealed.

caption: The host sees only ciphertext. The network says no.
narration: Here's everything we, the host, can see. Ciphertext. Steal the whole database, try to decrypt it, and the network says no.

caption: One admin signs: 1 of 2. Stuck. Even the master admin can't force it.
narration: Now an insider. Helix's admin proposes unsealing the room and signs it himself. One of two. Stuck. Even our master admin key can't force it.

caption: Second institution co-signs: 2 of 3. Quorum. The room opens.
narration: St Aurelia's admin reviews it and co-signs in her own enclave. Two of three. Quorum. The treaty opens the room.

caption: Everyone's results open at the same moment.
narration: Back to Mei: everyone's results open at the same moment. Nobody went first, nobody got scooped.

title: No single party holds the key
caption: The key never exists in one piece.
Every request is checked. Access changes only with a quorum of enclave signatures.
narration: Why TideCloak? The key never exists in one piece. Tide's nodes check every request, and access changes only with a quorum of enclave signatures.

subtitle: We built it, and we can't read it or open it alone.
note: This walkthrough simulates the Tide network calls, because Tide's public nodes were down while we recorded. The live code is in the repo.
